steps.title: Problem overview and goals
steps.content: Design a Parts Compatibility feature that answers: given a product (make/model/year or SKU), which parts are compatible? Goals: fast (sub-100ms) lookup for UI, accurate relationships for cross-references, support bulk checks, and simple operational workflows for updating compatibility data. Consider correctness vs latency tradeoffs and how to represent complex rules (fitment tables, vehicle attributes, optional trims).

steps.title: User journeys & API surface
steps.content: Primary flows: (1) Customer enters vehicle or part number and sees a filtered list of compatible parts; (2) Admin uploads bulk compatibility CSV/feeds; (3) Merchants inspect cross-reference data. Minimal public API: POST /compatibility/query (single or bulk), GET /parts/{sku}/compatibility, POST /compatibility/import. Include pagination, filtering, and confidence flags for fuzzy matches.

component.highlightReason: Public API for queries, bulk imports, and admin operations.
component.label: Compatibility API

properties.description: HTTP API exposing single and bulk compatibility queries, admin import endpoints, and search-backed cross-references.

steps.title: Add the Compatibility API
steps.content: API validates input (make/model/year or SKU), enforces auth for admin imports, and routes queries to the Compatibility Service or Search when appropriate. Bulk imports are accepted asynchronously with a job id for status polling.

component.highlightReason: Core service that evaluates compatibility rules and orchestrates lookups.
component.label: Compatibility Service

properties.description: Service implementing rule engine, graph traversals, precomputed matrices and fallback heuristics. Exposes internal lookup APIs consumed by the API and bulk processors.

steps.title: Add the Compatibility Service
steps.content: This service centralizes compatibility logic: exact matches via graph lookups, rule evaluation for conditional fitment (e.g., trim-level exceptions), and score-based fallbacks when data is incomplete. Keep rule evaluation deterministic and testable.

component.highlightReason: Natural fit to model parts, vehicles, and fitment relationships.
component.label: Graph DB (Neo4j)

properties.description: Stores nodes for SKUs, vehicle variants, attributes and edges for compatibility relationships. Efficient traversal for indirect compatibility queries.

steps.title: Add the Graph Database
steps.content: Use labeled nodes (Part, Vehicle, Trim) and relationship types (fits, replaces, supersedes). Precompute common paths or ancestors for very frequent queries to reduce traversal time.

connection.description: API forwards validated queries to the Compatibility Service for evaluation.
connection.label: API → Compatibility Service

steps.title: API → Compatibility Service (query routing)
steps.content: Route single-item queries to the Compatibility Service synchronously; accept bulk requests and return a job id after handing them off to the bulk processor.

connection.description: Service performs graph traversals and pattern matches against the graph store.
connection.label: Compat Service → Graph DB

steps.title: Compatibility Service → Graph DB (fitment lookup)
steps.content: Use parameterized traversal queries and pagination for large result sets. Push heavy path searches to background jobs if needed.

component.highlightReason: Search to support SKU lookup, fuzzy matching and front-end filtering.
component.label: Search Index (Elasticsearch)

properties.description: Indexed SKU metadata and vehicle attribute documents for fast filtering, text search and faceted navigation.

steps.title: Add Search Index (Elasticsearch)
steps.content: Keep search for fast SKU suggestions, attribute filters (make/model/year) and cross-reference lookups. Use index-time enrichment from the graph for frequently used computed fields.

connection.description: Search service provides SKU suggestions and filter results to the API for UI responsiveness.
connection.label: API → Search

steps.title: API → Search (suggestions & filters)
steps.content: Prefer search for lightweight queries and the UI list rendering; defer graph traversal for deeper compatibility checks or authoritative answering when needed.

component.highlightReason: Cache results for hot vehicle+SKU lookups to achieve sub-100ms UI latency.
component.label: Compatibility Cache (Redis)

properties.description: Stores recent query results and precomputed compatibility matrices for fast read paths.

steps.title: Add the Cache (Redis)
steps.content: Cache authoritative compatibility responses for popular vehicles or SKUs. Invalidate or update entries when ingestion publishes changes.

connection.description: Service writes computed results to cache and reads cache before falling back to graph/search.
connection.label: Compat Service ↔ Cache

steps.title: Compatibility Service → Cache (read/write)
steps.content: Read-through and write-through cache patterns reduce graph load. Use TTLs and explicit invalidation on updates.

component.highlightReason: Ingests vendor feeds, CSV uploads and background updates into the graph store.
component.label: Compatibility ETL

properties.description: Parses feeds, normalizes SKUs, applies mapping rules and writes edges/nodes into the graph. Emits change events for downstream indexing and cache invalidation.

steps.title: Add the Data Ingestion Pipeline (ETL)
steps.content: Design ingest jobs to be idempotent and report per-row errors. Maintain provenance metadata to allow rollbacks or manual correction.

connection.description: ETL writes normalized nodes/edges and emits change events.
connection.label: ETL → Graph DB

steps.title: ETL → Graph DB (write feed updates)
steps.content: Use batched writes and bulk import APIs where possible to accelerate large updates. Emit fine-grained events so search and cache can stay consistent.

component.highlightReason: Handles large bulk compatibility checks and re-computation tasks.
component.label: Bulk Processor

properties.description: Worker pool for bulk SKU compatibility checks, reindex windows, and expensive graph traversals that can't be synchronous.

steps.title: Add the Bulk Processor
steps.content: Bulk jobs run asynchronously, update the graph and emit cache invalidations. Provide job monitoring and restart semantics for failed batches.

connection.description: Bulk worker writes results and corrections to the graph database.
connection.label: Bulk → Graph DB

steps.title: Bulk Processor → Graph DB (batch updates)
steps.content: Ensure bulk writes are idempotent and instrumented. Large reprocessing windows should be throttled to avoid degrading online query latency.

component.highlightReason: Decouples ingest, indexing, and cache invalidation workflows.
component.label: Event Bus (Kafka)

properties.description: Streams change events from ETL and bulk processors to consumers that update search indices and caches.

steps.title: Add Message Broker (Kafka)
steps.content: Publish fine-grained change events (node/edge upserts, deletes). Consumers will update search indices and trigger targeted cache invalidations.

connection.description: ETL publishes normalized change events so downstream systems can react asynchronously.
connection.label: ETL → Event Bus

steps.title: ETL → Event Bus (publish changes)
steps.content: Asynchronous events allow near-real-time updates to search and cache without coupling ingest latency to user queries.

connection.description: Consumers apply events to graph and search stores and emit cache invalidations.
connection.label: Event Bus → Consumers

steps.title: Event Bus → Graph & Search (consumers)
steps.content: Consumers should be idempotent and designed for retries. Use transactional outbox patterns when the origin system must guarantee delivery.

steps.title: Matching strategies and trade-offs
steps.content: Trade-offs: precompute compatibility matrices for top-N vehicles to get O(1) reads vs compute-on-demand with graph traversals for correctness. Use hybrid: cache precomputed results for popular vehicles/SKUs and fall back to graph traversal for rare queries. For complex rules, run rule engine in a deterministic order and surface confidence scores to the UI.

steps.title: Scaling, caching and latency targets
steps.content: Strategies: shard graph by vehicle segment or tenant, keep hot partitions in memory, use Redis for sub-100ms reads, and autoscale Compatibility Service based on queue depth. Measure P50/P95 latency, cache hit ratio, and stale result rates after ingestion. Aim for 95th percentile < 200ms on UI queries.

steps.title: MVP implementation plan
steps.content: Stage 1: Build API + Compatibility Service, wire Graph DB with a small sample feed, and return exact matches. Stage 2: Add Search index and Redis cache for UI. Stage 3: Implement ETL and event bus for incremental updates. Stage 4: Add bulk processor, monitoring, and expanded scale testing.

steps.title: Acceptance criteria and benchmarks
steps.content: Acceptance: (1) Single SKU compatibility lookup returns correct set for 99% of test cases; (2) UI latency p95 < 200ms at target load; (3) Bulk import processes N records/hour and reports per-row errors; (4) Cache invalidation ensures fresh results within 60s after a data update.
